title: feat(plugin-auth): a platform admin can read the address the allowed IP ranges save check will judge (#30398)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgBMFd7n39sLWSMN4mnBtvAW)_

domain:server#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CZbTJpa9PNbpp3fdB7

Fixes #30398

Clause-②: yes (widening) — a new authenticated HTTP read, `GET /api/v1/auth/admin/client-address`, ledgered `server-only` in the plugin's auth route ledger; no spec schema, SDK method or package export moves.
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：新增一个只读接口 `GET /api/v1/auth/admin/client-address`，平台管理员在保存「允许的 IP 段」之前，就能看到服务器会拿哪个地址去判（`clientAddress`），以及是否信任代理转发头（`trustProxy`）。
- 为什么改：这个地址以前只出现在保存被拒的提示里，管理员只有先被拒一次才知道服务器认的是哪个地址；控制台也不能自己猜，因为放在代理后面时浏览器看到的地址不是服务器判的那个。
- 风险与回滚：只加不改。地址取自保存校验自己的那一次调用，两边不会说法不一；只有平台管理员能读，未登录 401、非管理员 403，匿名的 `/config` 不变；响应带 `no-store`。保存校验和登录闸门的判法一字未变。回滚即撤本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.ts` 的 `judgedClientAddress`（两扇门共用的取址）；`client-address-read.ts`（接口本体）；`allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts` 末尾 `#30398` 用例（同一连接分别问接口和保存，结果逐字相等）；两个 dogfood 的 `/admin/` 路由清点各加一行归类。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts`，预期 1 个文件、21 条全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

**The rule: the address shown to an administrator before a save is the address that save is judged by, because both come from one call.**

- **`judgedClientAddress` (`allowed-ip-ranges.ts`).** The save check's inline call to `AuthManager.resolveClientAddress` moves into an exported helper: the request's peer address plus only the forwarded-address headers the rule reads (`FORWARDED_CLIENT_ADDRESS_HEADERS`, the narrowing the settings service already applies to the save check's input, so on that path it is idempotent), `server.trustProxy` read inside the manager as before. The save check calls it with the same input it had; its refusal copy is untouched. The transport type it takes, formerly the file-private `WriteTransport`, is exported as `RequestTransport` (package-internal: `allowed-ip-ranges.ts` is not on the package's `exports`).
- **`GET /api/v1/auth/admin/client-address` (`client-address-read.ts`, mounted in `auth-plugin.ts`).** Answers `200 { success: true, data: { clientAddress, trustProxy } }` with `Cache-Control: no-store`. `clientAddress` is `judgedClientAddress` on this request's headers and transport peer, in the rule's own text (an IPv4-mapped peer reads `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, as the save refusal's `constraint.clientAddress` names it), `null` when no address can be established. `trustProxy` is `AuthManager.trustsForwardedHeaders()`. Closed, empty query set: any parameter is refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` before the address is read (AGENTS.md route rule 5). No body is read.
- **Who may read it.** The shared `gateAdmin` every ObjectStack `/admin/*` auth mount calls (ADR-0068 D2 judge, `platform-admin-gate.ts`): no session `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`, a held session (ADR-0069 D3) `403` with the posture's code, any other non-platform-admin `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, each before the read runs. Not on the anonymous `GET /api/v1/auth/config`.
- **Ledger.** One `objectstack-mount` row, `server-only`, in `auth-route-ledger.ts`, and the conformance pin's hand-written objectstack set gains the route. `pnpm check:auth-mount-ledger`: 25 mounts, all accounted for.
- **The two `/admin/` route sweeps (dogfood).** A mounted `/admin/` route is in scope of both at once, so each classifies it: `admin-platform-admin-standing.dogfood.test.ts` lists it in `ADMITTED` (the platform admin is not refused), `admin-route-nonadmin-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` as `objectstack-gate` (anonymous `401`, member `403`, admin not refused). No payload is needed: nothing is read before the gate.
- **For the ui half (#30313 item 1).** Call `GET /api/v1/auth/admin/client-address` (same-origin, session cookie) on the Authentication settings page and show `data.clientAddress` beside the Allowed IP ranges field; `null` means the server cannot establish the address (any non-empty list would then be refused). A `403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED` from it means the caller's address is already outside the list in force (the D5 gate answers it, see Acceptance notes).
- Not changed: the save check's verdict and copy, the sign-in gate, `resolveClientAddress`, `service-settings`, `packages/spec`, the SDK.

## Why

#30398: the save check from #30309 refuses a list that leaves out the saving request's address and names it, but nothing served that address before a save, so an administrator learned it only by being refused, and the console had no correct way to show it (triage 6655147452: the served address must come from the function the save check judges with; the client never guesses its own address).

## Verification

Measured first, at `6fa842af`: no auth route, no `/api/v1/auth/config` field and no `GET /api/settings/auth` field answers `resolveClientAddress`; the save check (`allowed-ip-ranges.ts`) is its only settings-side caller. `get-session` serves the session row's `ip_address`, which is a different fact (see Acceptance notes).

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

`allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts` › `#30398` (the shared harness: real `AuthPlugin`, real `SettingsService` with the shipped auth manifest, real settings routes for the save, and now the plugin's real auth routes on a real Hono app for the read, the transport peer supplied the way `@hono/node-server` supplies it). Each address case asks the read and then saves `192.0.2.0/24` from the same connection, and asserts the read's `clientAddress` equals the refusal's `constraint.clientAddress`:

- direct peer `203.0.113.9`; IPv4-mapped peer `::ffff:127.0.0.1` (not rewritten to dotted); `trustProxy` declared with `X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.7, 10.0.0.2` (leftmost entry); `trustProxy` not declared with forged `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Real-IP` (the peer `10.0.0.1` at both doors); no peer at all (`null` at both doors).
- `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- refusals before any address is read (`trustsForwardedHeaders` never called, no `data`): no session `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`; a signed-in non-admin `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`; a held platform admin `403 MFA_REQUIRED`; an unknown query parameter `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

`auth-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts`: the objectstack-sourced set includes the route, and better-auth does not serve it.

That run is the red leg for the two classifications above; with them, both files pass (Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 15 passed (15)). On the final head `843cf4fe` (`main` `f273c9fe` merged, closure rebuilt): `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test` Test Files 224 passed (224), Tests 3964 passed | 10 skipped (3974); full dogfood under the verify lock (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test`, no shard), lock verdict `command-exit 0`: Test Files 419 passed | 3 skipped (422), Tests 3492 passed | 36 skipped (3528).

## Acceptance notes

- **Gate population.** The read uses the `/admin/*` family's one judge (platform admin), not a fresh `manage_platform_settings` check through the settings door's composition. With the shipped permission sets the two populations are the same callers: platform-admin standing is derived from holding `admin_full_access` (`resolveAuthzContext`), which carries `manage_platform_settings`, the `auth` namespace's read and write capability, and `organization_admin` withholds that capability. They part only at two edges: a custom permission set granting `manage_platform_settings` without `admin_full_access` may save but is refused the read (it loses only the hint; the save check still names the address), and the judge's legacy `role === 'admin'` fallback may read its own address without being able to save. Judging the settings capability exactly would mean re-composing the settings door's resolver call, held-session and outage relays inside plugin-auth, a second copy of a door; not done here.
- **The session row's address is not this address.** `get-session` serves `session.ipAddress`, stamped at sign-in in its canonical text (`client-address-canonical.ts`: an IPv4-mapped peer is stored dotted). It can differ from the current connection (the address changed since sign-in) and from the judged text, so it was not reused; ablation A2 pins the text difference.
- **The read is behind the allow-list in force.** It sits under the auth mount, where the ADR-0069 D5 middleware judges every route except `/config` and `/bootstrap-status`. A caller whose address is already outside the list in force gets `403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED` from the read; no exemption is added to the gate.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` › *Saving, clearing and lockout recovery* does not mention the read yet; it is outside this card's declared file surface. A one-line addition fits there once the ui half shows the address. Carrier: the seat.
- Serial: `allowed-ip-ranges.ts`'s refusal copy (`COPY`, `copyFor`) is byte-untouched, for this seat's #30385.
